newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products turn mixed, Turkey buys gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products turn mixed, Turkey buys gas oil.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Thursday with traders watching arbitrage opportunities in fuel oil and naphtha, traders said.
In gas oil, traders said heating oil premiums were weaker, offered at around cif high +$3 basis Genoa, down $2 from a week ago, and cif high +$1 basis Greece.

Traders said Turkish state-owned oil company Tupras bought about six cargoes totalling 135,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for delivery in the first half of December. At least two of the cargoes had already been covered, they added.
Traders said Onyx was awarded about 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes at fob high +$10.50 cif Samsun, two 25,000 tonne cargoes at fob high +$11.50 cif Tutunciflik.
Total won a cargo at fob high +$13.75 cif Mersin, Tempotrade a cargo at fob high +$13.68 cif Iskanderun and Penta a cargo at fob Med mean +$2 fob Bulgaria.
Fuel oil was firmer with continuing strong U.S. natural gas prices and arbitrage interest.
Italy's purchase of up 250,000 tonnes from the low sulphur spot market this week also helped buoy sentiment, although trade was thin on Thursday.
Arbitrage high sulphur buyers were bidding at least $110 fob Mediterranean, although most transatlantic trade was originating from the Baltic.

A Suez cargo loading on Nov 22 was thought to be heading to Italy, and valued at $4-5 premium to the cracked cif Med high, or $125 cif. Some traders said prices were being suppressed for short-term pricing reasons.
Tunisia's ETAP issued a purchase tender for 100,000 tonnes of 3.5 percent sulphur fuel oil for delivery over the first six months of 1997.
